description.narrative: Following the adoption of the National Wellness Policy by the Labour Advisory Board in Eswatini, Cabinet adopted the Policy and its accompanying implementation plan in October 2023. A tripartite approach applied in the formulation of both the National Wellness Workplace Policy and the accompanying implementation plan drew the engagement of representatives from Government, Organized Labour, and Business. The implementation plan of the Policy includes activities that provide for an enabling environment in the workplace that is non-discriminatory, safe, and healthy for all persons in the world of work and responds effectively to wellness matters. As it addresses issues of HIV and AIDS, the Policy and its implementation plan are primarily aligned to ILO Recommendation No.200. They are further aligned to ILO Conventions 111 on discrimination in respect of employment and occupation (Articles-4-and-5); C 155 on occupational health and safety (Articles 3-4-5); and C190 on violence and harassment in the world of work. In June 2023 the Government of Eswatini partnered with the Institute for Development Management to sensitize and train labour inspectors on the Wellness Workplace Policy, and to promote its sensitization amongst senior management in the private sector. The ILO supported and facilitated three training workshops for the Tripartite Technical Committee on Occupational Health and Safety (TCOSH) focusing on the concepts of Gender Equality, Inclusion, and relevant provisions of Convention 190 in April 2022, June 2022, and Feb 2023 respectively. The training was to enhance the capacity of the TCOSH to mainstream Gender, Inclusion and to integrate relevant provisions of C190 in the Implementation Plan of the Policy. In March 2023, the ILO collaborated with the Ministry of Labour and Social Security to convene a workshop with the Tripartite Technical Committee on Occupational Health and Safety (TCOSH) for the actual drafting of the implementation plan for the Wellness Workplace Policy. In June 2023, the ILO supported the Ministry of Labour and Social Security in addressing the comments on the first draft Implementation Plan for the Wellness Workplace Policy by the Eswatini Public Policy Coordination Unit (PPCU), ensuring that the implementation plan was amended accordingly before its resubmission

description.narrative: The Government of Eswatini completed the Social Security Inquiry exercise to improve the statistical system and data on social security . The SSI was completed and adopted by the Ministry of Labour & Social Security in July 2023. Information collected and compiled during the exercise provided valuable baseline data that is used and cited in the Eswatini National Development Plan 2023/24 – 27/28 and the Second National Voluntary Review Report issued by the Ministry of Economic Planning and Development. The SSI reveals gender disaggregated data of recipients of various social protection measures such as the old age grant, private and foreign retirement funds, contributory old age pensions, the free primary education programme, and the OVC education grant, among others. In the previous biennium (2020-2021) with the support of RBSA the ILO facilitated training on the SSI for 2 social security practitioners – one from the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MOLSS) and another from the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) – as well as a government consultant. The focus of training was to orientate the officials on the concept of the ILO’s SSI and on the practical application of the ILO’s Webtool for the filling in of relevant data in the SSI. In August 2022 additional training was provided for the two officers from the MOLSS and the ENPF to highlight the strategic importance of keeping updated social security data. The training emphasized the inclusion of data on migrant workers in all social protection schemes and to ensure that member states are treat equally as national citizens.
